name: Hadadezer
description: King living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David smote Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates, taking a thousand chariots, seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen, houghing the chariot horses but reserving a hundred chariots.

When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer, he sent his son Joram to salute and bless David, because Hadadezer had had wars with Toi. Joram brought vessels of silver, gold, and brass.
David dedicated the silver and gold to the Lord, along with that dedicated from all the nations he subdued: Syria, Moab, the children of Ammon, the Philistines, Amalek, and the spoil of Hadadezer.

When all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw they were smitten before Israel, they made peace and served them, and the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon anymore. This is what happens when you mess with the armies of the living God: they got whooped so badly that the Syrians would not even help the Ammonites anymore.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: David smote the Philistines and subdued them, took Moab, and struck Hadarezer king of Zobah as he went to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 18: The Victories of King David

points: Tou king of Hamath heard how David had smitten the host of Hadarezer and sent his son to greet David and congratulate him.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 18: The Victories of King David

points: The beaten Syrians called for reinforcements from beyond the river under Shophach, captain of Hadarezer's host.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 19: War With Ammon and Syria

points: The servants of Hadarezer made peace with David and became his servants, and the Syrians would no longer help Ammon; they wanted nothing more to do with David and the mighty men.
